description: SSE frame parsing. `chunks` are the byte groups exactly as the transport would deliver them (an arbitrary split is part of the test). \r and \n are literal escapes. events[] is what must be dispatched, in order. A parser that reads line-by-line without buffering will pass most of these by accident - the split-chunk cases are the ones that catch it.

cases.name: minimal event, LF terminated
CRLF line endings
CR-only line endings
one frame split across three chunks
the blank line between frames may be split so that only its LF lands in a chunk
CRLF terminator split across the chunk boundary
multi-line data joins with a single newline
exactly one space after the colon is stripped, extra spaces are kept
chunks:
data:  two leading spaces
data:one
data:

cases.name: comment/heartbeat lines are ignored but must not swallow the event after them
a lone heartbeat frame with a trailing blank line dispatches nothing
event with no data field dispatches nothing (spec: empty data buffer -> do not dispatch)
unknown fields are ignored
field with no colon is treated as a field with an empty value, which still fills the data buffer
id and retry are captured; retry is milliseconds
retry with a non-integer value is ignored, the connection keeps its own schedule
an id containing NUL is ignored, so last_event_id stays at the previous value
two frames arriving in one chunk
stream ends with a half frame: it must not be dispatched
a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across the chunk boundary must not garble
Komga-shaped payload: data carries the whole JSON object with the entity id
